findings.evidence: Probe with an injected MockTransport returning 200, text/html and content-encoding gzip: FetchUrlTool returns {'status': 'unsupported', 'message': "URI has no reader for content type 'unknown'.", 'content_type': ''}. SafeFetcher asks for Accept-Encoding: identity and sets UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT_TYPE without recording the content type. The old requests path decompressed transparently. Smaller related changes on public fetches: the Accept header no longer lists PDF/DOCX/XLSX (requests sent */*); the User-Agent changed; HTML without a header charset now defaults to UTF-8 (or the meta charset), not ISO-8859-1, so a Latin-1 'café' becomes 'caf�'.
findings.suggested_fix: In fetch_url, report a content-encoding refusal as 'could not read that page (compressed response)', or record content_type before returning. Optionally add */* or the document MIME types to the Accept header used for fetch_url.
findings.title: A public page sent with Content-Encoding gzip is now reported as 'unsupported, content type unknown'; requests used to decompress it

findings.evidence: _REFUSAL_MESSAGES maps HOST_NUMERIC_AMBIGUOUS to _PRIVATE_MESSAGE. A public obfuscated form such as http://0x5db8d70e/ (93.184.215.14) is refused as 'URI will not fetch that address (private or local network).' This is the same kind of wrong-reason wording as R1-01, in a narrower case.
findings.suggested_fix: Map HOST_NUMERIC_AMBIGUOUS to e.g. 'URI only fetches host names or standard dotted IP addresses.'
findings.title: HOST_NUMERIC_AMBIGUOUS (and proxy-only HOST_SINGLE_LABEL) are worded 'private or local network' even when the address is public
